problem: Which of the following is equivalent to ${\int }_{C}({x}^{2}-8{y}^{2})\,\text{d}s,$ where $C$ is the ellipse ${x}^{2}+8{y}^{2}=8,$ traversed once in the counterclockwise direction?

activity_context.topic_title: Line Integrals of Scalar Functions Over Ellipses

examples.knowledge_point: Constructing the Line Integral of a Function Over an Ellipse
examples.problem: What expression is equivalent to $\displaystyle \int_\limits{C} \dfrac{x}{y} \: \textrm{d}s,$ where $C$ is the ellipse $x^2 + 16y^2 = 16,$ traversed once in the counterclockwise direction?
examples.worked_solution:
We will use the formula

$$
\int\limits_C f(x, y) \, \textrm{d}s  = \int\limits_a^b  f(\mathbf r(t)) \, \| \mathbf r'(t) \| \, \textrm{d}t.
$$

 

Note that we can write the equation of our ellipse in the form

$$
\dfrac{x^2}{4^2} + \dfrac{y^2}{1^2} = 1.
$$

So, the curve $C$ is an ellipse centered at $O$ with horizontal and vertical semiaxes of $4$ and $1,$ respectively. Therefore, it can be parametrized as 

$$
\mathbf{r}(t) = \left\langle 4\cos{t}, \: \sin{t} \right\rangle, \qquad 0 \le t \lt 2\pi.
$$

Computing $\mathbf{r}'(t)$ and $\| \mathbf{r}'(t) \|,$ we get following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4\operatorname{cos}⁡t)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t)j \\  & =-4\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(-4\operatorname{sin}⁡t)^{2}+(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{16{sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t} \\  & =\sqrt{15{sin}^{2}⁡t+({sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t)} \\  & =\sqrt{15{sin}^{2}⁡t+1}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $f(x,y) = \dfrac{x}{y},$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(t)) & =\frac{4\operatorname{cos}⁡t}{\operatorname{sin}⁡t}=4\operatorname{cot}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write the integral as

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}\frac{x}{y}\,\text{d}s & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }f(r(t))\,‖{r}^{′}(t)‖\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }4\operatorname{cot}⁡t\sqrt{15{sin}^{2}⁡t+1}\,\text{d}t \\  & =4{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }\operatorname{cot}⁡t\sqrt{15{sin}^{2}⁡t+1}\,\text{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$
